title: Refactor AZ-aware EIP allocation and NAT failover workflows to reduce cross-AZ egress and simplify IaC
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Our current Terraform networking templates allocate Elastic IPs and NAT gateways using a cluster-level pattern that often forces cross-AZ egress during failover and creates ongoing drift in per-environment state files. This causes increased egress cost, harder-to-reproduce networking diffs, and frequent manual fixes when regions scale or AZ mappings change.

Goal: Refactor Terraform modules and templates so that: (1) EIP allocation is AZ-scoped and namespaced per environment, (2) NAT gateway failover uses an explicit AZ-aware route priority instead of ad-hoc re-creation, and (3) the module surface exposes a cheaper NAT instance option for low-throughput dev/staging environments. The change should be backwards-compatible for existing workspaces with a clear migration path and automated state moves where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: New terraform module `networking/az_nat` created and documented in module registry
Per-AZ EIP allocation implemented with stable resource names to avoid unpredictable replacements
Migration plan documented and a tfstate move script created for < 30GB-environments
Integration tests run in staging that simulate AZ failover and validate no cross-AZ SNAT traffic is introduced
Cost model demonstrates >= 12% egress cost reduction in sample prod-like workload when NAT instances used for dev/staging
Rollout runbook with canary steps, health checks, and rollback instructions published in Confluence
checklist: Design RFC describing module interface and migration strategy
Prototype in sandbox account and validate provider v5.x behavior
Create module unit tests and terratest scenario for failover
Open GitHub PR with module and template changes
Coordinate with Platform SRE for staged rollout
Schedule cutover window and communicate to impacted teams
